purpose.summary: Expose the first upstream-compatible Chronik HTTP token route over the accepted confirmed-token index, on explicit loopback-only local-regtest opt-in.
scope: Serve GET /token/:txid with the canonical application/x-protobuf TokenInfo representation and upstream-compatible protobuf errors.
Own the HTTP service inside the default-off persistent runtime and stop it before the database closes.
Bind the listener to an explicit loopback address and keep all node validation and chain-selection authority outside Chronik.
Exercise confirmed ALP metadata, malformed and missing queries, rollback, reconsideration and restart persistence in a native functional test.
exclusions: No full Chronik server, transaction route, mempool query, UTXO query, history, websocket, plugin, wallet or public-network service is added.
No consensus, validation, activation, chain-selection, P2P, network-identity or mainnet parameter behavior changes.
No private source, history, operator data, incoming evidence, binary, cache, build output or host-specific path is tracked.

commands: Build the standalone node with all Chronik options OFF.
expected_results: No Chronik listener or route is linked or registered and node behavior remains unchanged.

commands: Build bitcoind with BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=ON and leave runtime observer opt-in disabled.
expected_results: No database or listening socket is opened.

commands: Run the locked Rust corpus and feature_chronik_token_http.py against a native observer build.
expected_results: The explicit loopback route serves canonical confirmed token metadata and remains isolated from node correctness.

scenarios.command: Run the asset observer and token HTTP scenarios with explicit local-regtest observer opt-in and an explicit loopback -chronikbind.
expected_results: ALP genesis returns canonical TokenInfo and malformed or missing token IDs return canonical protobuf errors.
failure_conditions: Implicit listener, non-loopback listener, incorrect content type, wrong protobuf, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Restart the explicit local-regtest index and repeat the confirmed HTTP token query.
expected_results: The token and canonical block metadata remain readable after restart.
failure_conditions: Missing token, metadata drift, listener failure, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run the existing full-reindex observer scenario before querying confirmed metadata.
expected_results: A rebuilt index returns the same canonical confirmed token representation.
failure_conditions: Stale state, incomplete rebuild, query divergence, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run the existing chainstate-reindex observer scenario before querying confirmed metadata.
expected_results: Ordered callbacks rebuild queryable state without changing chain selection.
failure_conditions: Stale state, node-authority effect, query divergence, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Run the existing pruned-datadir observer scenario.
expected_results: Unavailable history disables only persistence and cannot leave a contradictory served view.
failure_conditions: Node shutdown, silent stale query, validation effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

scenarios.command: Invalidate and reconsider the token block, then exercise the existing deep-reorganization failure boundary.
expected_results: Rolled-back token metadata is absent, restored metadata returns exactly and deeper contradictions remain isolated to indexing.
failure_conditions: Stale token response, missing restored response, node-authority effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

limitations: Only confirmed token genesis metadata is served; mempool state, transaction queries, UTXOs, histories, websockets and plugins remain outside this slice.
The listener is intentionally restricted to explicit loopback local-regtest use and is not a deployment contract.
The local macOS run is a component observation only; public CI and review are still pending.
counterevidence: The first native configuration encountered an inherited MiniUPnPc 2.3.3 API incompatibility; the governed wallet-, ZMQ- and UPnP-off Chronik CI profile built successfully without changing production source for that unrelated dependency.

The linker reported that locally compiled RocksDB objects target macOS 26.5 while the node target is macOS 26.0; linking completed and the native functional tests passed, but public Ubuntu CI remains authoritative for this change.
A requested token service that cannot bind is deliberately disabled without affecting validation or node startup, preserving observer isolation.
